item.title: ECB to pause today before delivering next and final rate hike in September - Deutsche
item.description:
The ECB is expected to keep policy unchanged today while reaffirming a data dependent and/or meeting-by-meeting approach. There shouldn't be much else to it honestly.

The statement language is expected to remain the same and so the only thing to watch for is Lagarde's press conference. But even then, she will just reaffirm potential upside risks to the inflation outlook as well as downside risks to the economic outlook. I wouldn't expect much more than that.

The inflation numbers in June pretty much gave policymakers what they needed to pause in July. As such, the scrutiny on policy setting will be deferred to the September meeting next. And that is when Deutsche anticipates the ECB to deliver their next and final rate hike. The firm notes that:

"A pause in July is expected. Current oil prices remain below 11 June levels, and the June HICP inflation data, which came in softer than expected, cast some doubt on the rapid emergence of indirect inflation. Furthermore, our June dbDIG survey indicated a complete unwinding of the initial energy shock's impact on household inflation expectations. Waiting until September will provide the ECB with two additional HICP prints and updated staff forecasts, enabling a more informed decision.
We continue to anticipate a second and final hike to 2.50% in September. In the July press conference, we expect the ECB to maintain neutral communications. This implies no explicit forward guidance, emphasizing a data- dependent, meeting-by-meeting approach without pre-committing to a specific policy path. While the communication will be neutral, we believe the ECB's tone on inflation will still convey a hawkish stance, consistent with a further 25bp hike in September being highly probable."

As much as the central bank might want to leave the door open to hike in September next, I would not expect Lagarde to make any promises or pre-commitments in her press conference later. As such, the meeting decision today should be a non-event. And if so, that means the ECB will have done its job properly before breaking for the summer.

This article was written by Justin Low at investinglive.com.

item.title: EUR/USD close to a major breakout as traders await the ECB decision, US-Iran developments
item.description:
FUNDAMENTAL OVERVIEW

 

USD:

The US dollar started to regain ground in recent days as the prolonged US-Iran conflict and surging oil prices trumped the hopes for a quick de-escalation. The situation in the Middle East is getting even worse as the Houthis started to disrupt the Bab el-Mandeb strait and the Red Sea. There’s still no end in sight to this crisis and the risk sentiment remains negative.

Given this backdrop, we saw a hawkish repricing across the board with the total Fed tightening now standing around 43 bps by year-end, compared to 32 bps last week after the soft US inflation data. The chances for a rate hike at the upcoming meeting in July have also risen back to 33%.

The US-Iran conflict will continue to support the US dollar amid the Fed tightening risk and negative risk sentiment. Traders will watch out for signs of de-escalation as that could trigger a dovish repricing and weigh on the greenback.

EUR:

On the EUR side, the ECB is expected to leave interest rates unchanged today while reiterating that it remains well positioned to navigate the uncertainty caused by the war and that it will continue to follow a data-dependent and meeting-by-meeting approach.

The central bank will not release the macroeconomic projections at this meeting, so the market focus will be mainly on President Lagarde's press conference for clues on whether policymakers are preparing for another rate hike in September.

The most likely scenario is that we get the usual post-meeting media "leak" signalling a rate hike in September if inflation data were to surprise to the upside. The market is pricing in a total of 47 bps of tightening by year-end (roughly two rate hikes) and a 73% chance of an increase at the next meeting in September.

Given this backdrop, it's going to be hard for Lagarde to out-hawk the market. Overall, the decision is likely to be a non-event with risks skewed to the downside for the euro. A pushback against the market pricing would trigger a selloff, while a pledge to tighten more than expected will likely lead to a short-term rally.

 

EURUSD TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – DAILY TIMEFRAME

On the daily chart, we can see that EURUSDbounced from the key support zone around the 1.14 handle and it continues to compress below the trendline. The sellers will likely step in around the trendline with a defined risk above it to position for a drop into the 1.13 handle. The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking higher to open the door for a rally into the 1.16 handle next.

EURUSD TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – 4 HOUR TIMEFRAME

On the 4 hour chart, we have an upward trendline defining the recent correction. The buyers will likely continue to lean on the trendline with a defined risk below it to keep targeting a break above the major trendline. The sellers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking below the trendline and the support to pile in for a drop into the 1.13 handle next.

EURUSD TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – 1 HOUR TIMEFRAME

On the 1 hour chart, there’s not much we can add here as the sellers will either wait for a break below the support or a pullback into the downward trendline. The buyers, on the other hand, will continue to step in around the upward trendline and wait for a break above the downward trendline to increase the bullish bets into new highs. The red lines define the average daily range for today.

UPCOMING CATALYSTS

Today, we have the ECB policy decision and the US Jobless Claims data, while tomorrow we conclude the week with the Eurozone and US Flash PMIs. The focus remains on US-Iran headlines.

item.title: US Secretary Rubio says price on Iran will get higher every night until they come to their senses
item.description:
• Iran begging us every day to make a deal
  • Looks like Iran not ready to make a deal, they will pay the price
  • Price on Iran will get higher every night until they come to their senses
  • Iran probably not ready to do a deal, but will be probably soon
  • Despite Iran's bravado, they are suffering tremendously and will continue to suffer
  • Think they will be ready for a deal soon
  • US is seeking a denuclearised Iran

The remarks come as the US and Iran continue exchanging military strikes following the collapse of the ceasefire earlier this month. The US has carried out nightly airstrikes targeting Iranian military infrastructure, while Iran has responded with missile and drone attacks against US-linked assets across the region and has continued threatening shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, and now the Red Sea via the Houthis.

The US maintains the diplomacy while simultaneously increasing military and economic pressure on Iran to force them in accepting their conditions. Rubio's comments suggest the US intends to continue intensifying pressure until Iran changes its negotiating stance as the administration sees sustained military operations and economic pressure as leverage to force Iran back to the negotiating table.

However, with both sides continuing daily exchanges of strikes and neither showing signs of backing down, prospects for a near-term diplomatic breakthrough remain low. Meanwhile, oil prices continue to surge with no top in sight.

This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

item.title: BOE rate hike bets ramp up as gilt yields surge higher
item.description:
With much focus on the bond market again this week, we're seeing UK yields push up significantly today. 10-year gilt yields have now climbed by over 4 bps to 5.08% - its highest in over two months. For some context, yields were only at 4.72% at the end of June.

The push higher comes as we're seeing inflation expectations build up amid higher energy prices, with that translating to a more hawkish BOE outlook as well.

As things stand, traders are now pricing in ~48 bps of rate hikes from the BOE by year-end. And that is quite a step up from ~20 bps a month ago and even from the ~36 bps priced in last week.

The obvious factor as what is also affecting the global bond market and also major central bank expectations is renewed tensions between US and Iran. And the fact that the war might even lead towards shipping disruption in the Red Sea only serves to exacerbate the supply disruption in energy markets. That narrative is very much well reflected by the resurgence in oil prices in recent weeks with WTI crude on the verge of touching $90 again with Brent crude also eyeing the $100 mark.

But in the case of the UK, fiscal worries are starting to come back into the picture. The bond vigilantes look to be coming back, especially after a mess of a first policy announcement by the Burnham administration. From earlier this week:

  • Trouble already for Burnham in his first policy announcement?
  • UK prime minister Burnham announces VAT cut from energy bills to bring down cost of living

As such, that's leading to pressure on multiple fronts on the gilts market. It's not inflation concerns that is driving yields higher, but also the fact that investors are demanding a higher yield premium to hold UK sovereign debt amid fiscal worries. Pain.

This article was written by Justin Low at investinglive.com.

item.title: ECB preview: High bar for the ECB to out-hawk the market; September hike likely if inflation surprises to the upside
item.description:
The ECB is widely expected to leave interest rates unchanged today, while reiterating that it remains well positioned to navigate the uncertainty caused by the war and that it will continue to follow a data-dependent and meeting-by-meeting approach. The central bank will not release the macroeconomic projections at this meeting, so the market focus will be mainly on President Lagarde's press conference for clues on whether policymakers are preparing for another rate hike in September.

The case for a pause has strengthened over recent weeks. Eurozone inflation moderated in June, services inflation surprised to the downside, wage growth continued to soften, and inflation expectations remained relatively well anchored. Business surveys have also pointed to sluggish economic activity, suggesting the ECB can afford to wait for additional evidence before tightening policy further.

Recent comments from ECB members have struck a measured tone, acknowledging that higher oil prices represent an upside risk to inflation while adding that the feared second-round effects through wages have yet to materialize. Several members have highlighted the absence of sustained wage pressures, reinforcing the argument for more patience.

Unfortunately, the upside risks for inflation and downside risks for growth have increased again recently amid the renewed US-Iran conflict. Oil prices have climbed back above $90 per barrel with no top in sight amid disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, and now also the Red Sea. These risks are likely to keep the ECB's tightening bias intact.

As a result, traders expect today's decision to deliver a "hawkish" pause with President Lagarde reiterating that future decisions will continue to depend on incoming data, while keeping the door open to another rate increase if inflation risks intensify. The most likely scenario is that we get the usual post-meeting media "leak"signalling a rate hike in September if inflation data were to surprise to the upside.

The market is pricing in a total of 47 bps of tightening by year-end (roughly two rate hikes) and a 73% chance of an increase at the next meeting in September. Given this backdrop, it's going to be hard for Lagarde to out-hawk the market. Overall, the decision is likely to be a non-event and only a pushback against the market pricing or a pledge to tighten more than expected would trigger significant moves in the markets. 

This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

item.title: Alphabet earnings reaction cools an otherwise selective earnings season
item.description:
Alphabet shares traded near $333.76 following Wednesday night’s earnings, about 2.4% below the regular-session close of $341.91. The decline adds another negative mega-cap reaction to an earnings season that has become more selective, rather than uniformly bearish.

The important distinction for traders is that Alphabet’s decline appears more significant because of the company’s enormous market capitalization than because of the percentage move itself. Even a relatively contained fall in Alphabet can weigh heavily on the Nasdaq and on market-cap-weighted earnings sentiment.

In my technical chart analysis, I'm watching gold futures remaining stuck between 4,116 support and 4,145 resistance, where price continues to churn around developing VWAP near 4,127 as traders await a clean directional breakout. This consolidation comes against a backdrop of escalating geopolitical headlines; as Justin Low from investingLive.com reported, China's live-fire military drills in the Taiwan Strait are injecting fresh cross-asset volatility into the market.

Equity sentiment remains fragmented across regions. In my index breakdown, Nasdaq futures give bears a slight advantage below 29,195 following Alphabet's post-earnings pullback.

Conversely, Eamonn Sheridan at investingLive.com noted that Google's boosted AI capex guidance sparked a 3% surge in the Kospi and gains in the Nikkei as Asian semiconductor suppliers rallied. Rounding out today's market drivers, Giuseppe Dellamotta from investingLive.com outlined the main economic events for today, including the ECB rate decision and US jobless claims, which should serve as key macroeconomic catalysts for active traders.

Yesterday’s earnings tape sent mixed signals

The July 22 earnings session had two very different phases.

Before the market opened, the earnings tape was constructive. Positive reactions in companies such as Philip Morris, AT&T, CME Group and Westinghouse Air Brake Technologies supported a positive BMO earnings-regime reading. Breadth was also favorable, meaning the strength was not confined to one company.

The after-hours session was less supportive.

Tesla and Texas Instruments traded lower, while Alphabet’s subsequent decline added further pressure from mega-cap technology. These reactions did not necessarily represent extreme company-specific earnings shocks, but their combined index weight was enough to offset many smaller positive outcomes.

That leaves the broader earnings environment neutral to mildly defensive.

The market is still rewarding selected winners, including United Rentals, Medpace and several industrial and energy companies. However, investors are no longer providing automatic support to every large technology company that reports acceptable results.

Alphabet matters more to the index than to overall breadth

Alphabet’s reaction illustrates the difference between market-cap-weighted sentiment and equal-weight earnings breadth.

Equal-weight analysis asks how many companies are rising or falling and treats each reporter similarly. Market-cap-weighted analysis gives much greater influence to companies such as Alphabet and Tesla.

This can create a situation where:

  • More companies rise than fall.
  • Several smaller companies exceed their expected moves.
  • The Nasdaq still trades lower because one or two mega-cap companies decline.

That appears to be the main earnings message from Wednesday. The underlying earnings tape was not broadly weak, but the largest technology names were not providing enough leadership to generate a bullish index-level signal.

What traders can learn from the reaction

A negative earnings move is not automatically an earnings shock.

The severity of a reaction should be compared with the move that options markets had priced before the report. A stock falling 2% after earnings may be relatively contained when traders had expected a much larger move. Conversely, a 6% decline can be highly significant when the expected move was only 3%.

Market capitalization also matters. A modest decline in Alphabet can have more influence on the Nasdaq than a 15% rise in a much smaller company.

Finally, the initial gap is only the first stage of the earnings reaction. Traders should watch whether Alphabet:

  • Holds below its post-earnings price area.
  • Repairs the decline after the opening auction.
  • Establishes lower value and sustained selling pressure.
  • Recovers toward the previous close and rejects the bearish initial interpretation.

Earnings sentiment so far

The current earnings regime is best described as selective and mildly defensive.

There have been several strong winners, and many disappointments have remained within the moves already anticipated by options markets. At the same time, sharp declines in companies such as Intuitive Surgical, Danaher and MSCI, followed by softer reactions in Tesla and Alphabet, have prevented the earnings backdrop from becoming clearly bullish.

For traders, this favors company-specific analysis, relative-value trades and confirmation after the opening reaction. Broad conclusions based only on whether a company “beat” or “missed” are becoming less useful as the market increasingly focuses on valuation, guidance and the quality of future growth.

This article was written by Itai Levitan at investinglive.com.

item.title: French business climate brightens a little more as rebound extends into July

The latest reading comes amid an improvement in the business climate for both the manufacturing and services sectors, as well as in retail trade. The more detailed breakdown for the report is as per the following:

However, key risks remain as energy prices are starting to ramp higher again and that will only make things more complicated in the months ahead. That especially if the Middle East conflict continues to drag on for longer and also see a further disruption to shipping conditions in the Red Sea.

item.title: Gold analysis today shows price stuck in this range
item.description:
Gold price analysis: Futures remain trapped between 4,116 support and 4,145 resistance

Gold futures prediction score: -1

Gold futures are trading near 4,124 at the time of this analysis after failing to sustain Wednesday’s advance toward 4,171.

The broader recovery from below 4,000 remains visible, but the immediate structure has weakened. Price has fallen back beneath the developing VWAP and is rotating inside a compact value area between approximately 4,119 and 4,133.

That leaves gold in a short-term balance zone. A move within this area offers limited directional conviction, so traders may prefer to wait for price to leave the range before committing more aggressively.

Gold tradeCompass summary

  • Bullish above: 4,145
  • Bullish targets: 4,152, 4,160 and 4,168
  • Bearish below: 4,116
  • Bearish targets: 4,110, 4,104 and 4,093
  • Deeper bearish targets: 4,086 and 4,067
  • Prediction score: -1, neutral with a slight bearish lean

Why gold is currently neutral to slightly bearish

Gold produced an impressive advance from approximately 4,085 to 4,171, but the market could not maintain acceptance above 4,150.

The subsequent decline returned price to the 4,119-4,133 value area, where buyers and sellers are now competing for control. The developing VWAP near 4,127 also runs through this area, reinforcing the present lack of direction.

Another important observation is the rejection from Wednesday’s upper region. Gold reached 4,171 before declining toward 4,135 and subsequently printed an unusually deep intraday probe to 4,075. Although that decline was immediately repaired, it demonstrates that liquidity beneath the range can be vulnerable.

I'm currently tracking the order flow on Nasdaq futures, where bears are aggressively defending the 29,195 value area high following Alphabet's earnings, keeping our bullish tradeCompass scenario deactivated as the massive capital expenditures required to fund the AI race test buyer resolve. Until I see clear institutional absorption above that threshold, my short-term structural bias remains cautious, especially with escalating macro friction shaking risk appetite across the board.

As Eamonn Sheridan at investingLive.com just pointed out, the US deployment of a B-1 bomber against targets in Iran represents a massive strike escalation that is rapidly forcing a geopolitical risk premium back into crude oil prices. Compounding these global headwinds, Justin Low from our team noted that China is sending a clear message with new live-fire drills in the Taiwan Strait following recent diplomatic talks, creating the kind of sudden cross-asset volatility that requires us to stay rigidly disciplined around our intraday VWAP and point of control levels.

Bullish gold price scenario above 4,145

Gold becomes more constructive above 4,145.

This threshold is intentionally placed beyond the developing value area and recent overnight highs. A brief move above 4,133 or 4,140 would not be sufficient because price has already shown repeated two-way trading in that region.

If gold accepts above 4,145, bullish partial profit levels are:

  1. 4,152 - just before the previous session’s value area high near 4,152.4.
  2. 4,160 - an established resistance and prior breakout area.
  3. 4,168 - placed ahead of Wednesday’s 4,171.4 high to improve the probability of execution.

A sustained breakout beyond 4,171 would reopen the route toward approximately 4,180-4,188, but buyers first need to prove that the market can regain and hold the 4,145-4,152 resistance band.

Bearish gold price scenario below 4,116

The bearish tradeCompass activates below 4,116.

This level sits beneath the current value area low and near the previous session’s lower value boundary. A confirmed break would indicate that the market is no longer merely rotating around 4,124 and is beginning to accept lower prices.

Bearish partial profit levels are:

  1. 4,110 - the first nearby support and a sensible location for reducing risk.
  2. 4,104 - placed just above the 4,100 psychological level and Tuesday’s breakout area.
  3. 4,093 - positioned ahead of the previous 4,092.5 intraday high and nearby support.

If selling accelerates, 4,086 becomes the next downside magnet. The more important broader support remains near 4,067, where an earlier reference and a major portion of the recent advance originated.

The 4,116-4,145 no-trade zone

Between 4,116 and 4,145, gold remains vulnerable to repeated VWAP crossings and false breaks.

This does not mean no trade is possible inside the range. Experienced scalpers may still trade its edges, but the cleaner directional opportunity appears outside it:

  • Above 4,145, buyers regain the short-term advantage.
  • Below 4,116, sellers gain room to test 4,110, 4,104 and potentially 4,093.
  • Between those thresholds, neither side has established sufficient control.

Gold trade management

After the first partial profit target is reached, and certainly after the second, traders should consider moving the stop to entry or reducing risk aggressively. A remaining portion can then be left to pursue the deeper target, but a profitable trade should not be allowed to reverse into a full loss.

The levels above form a conditional price map, not a prediction that every target must be reached. Gold remains volatile, and traders should also account for contract size, slippage and their individual risk tolerance.

Trade at your own risk.

This article was written by Itai Levitan at investinglive.com.

item.title: China sends a clear message with live-fire drills in Taiwan Strait
item.description:
China has announced that it has begun live-fire drills in some ‌parts of the Taiwan Strait. The drills will run for two days and will be from 2200 GMT ​to 1000 GMT each day around the Dongshan Island, ‌bordering ⁠the province of Guangdong.

The timing of this move is very much all about sending a clear signal. It comes just a day after talks between US secretary of state Rubio and China foreign minister Wang Yi in Manila yesterday.

For some context, Rubio said that the US opposes China's deployment of coast guard vessels near Taiwan and also criticised the recent aggressive encroachments by Chinese coast guard ships into waters near Taiwan.

In his words, China was "undermining the spirit of strategic stability" while acknowledging that the deep policy differences on Taiwan will likely persist "for the foreseeable future". He also added that the pending US arms package to Taiwan is still under internal review.

And instead of fighting a war of words, evidently Beijing is sending a clear message with its actions today.

As a reminder, China held its most extensive war games encircling Taiwan back in ​December and that was right after the US unveiled a record $11.1 billion arms package for Taiwan.

So, it's fair to say that the timing of the latest live-fire drills is definitely not coincidental to say the least.

This article was written by Justin Low at investinglive.com.

item.title: Nasdaq analysis today shows Alphabet's slightly bearish reaction after its earnings gives bears a slight advantage
item.description:
Nasdaq futures analysis after Alphabet earnings: Bears hold an edge below 29,195

Nasdaq futures are attempting to stabilize near 29,100 after failing above 29,300, but the recovery is not yet strong enough to reverse the short-term bearish structure. The immediate decision zone is 29,020-29,195. A sustained break below 29,020 would favor another decline, while acceptance above 29,195 would begin a recovery that needs stronger confirmation above 29,220-29,260.

Key takeaways from today’s Nasdaq futures analysis

  • Short-term bias: Bearish, but approaching important support.
  • Nasdaq prediction score:-3 out of 10, with medium confidence.
  • Bullish threshold:29,195, with stronger confirmation above 29,220-29,260.
  • Bearish threshold:29,020, followed by the major structural test near 28,950.
  • Main resistance:29,295-29,365, where two recent rallies failed.
  • Alphabet earnings signal: Strong AI and cloud demand is supportive, but sharply higher capital spending and negative free cash flow are testing investors’ willingness to fund the AI race.
  • Practical interpretation: This is a decision area, not an attractive location to chase either direction before confirmation.

This analysis is based on September 2026 Nasdaq futures, commonly known as NQ. Traders using QQQ, Nasdaq 100 CFDs, index options or the cash index should treat the futures levels as market-structure references rather than exact execution prices.

I'm currently tracking the energy sector's order flow, where Brent crude has pushed past its Value Area High to test heavy resistance near $96 a barrel. As Eamonn Sheridan at investingLive.com reported, escalating US strikes in Iran and a Houthi blockade are pushing a massive geopolitical risk premium into crude, driving aggressive intraday bids. Despite this macro friction, I need to see if tech equities can sustain their structural momentum following a dominant Asian session. According to Eamonn's equity breakdown, Google's upward revision to its AI capex guidance is aggressively lifting Asian chipmakers, sparking a 3% gap-up in the Kospi as institutional buyers step in to absorb supply in names like SK Hynix.

With these cross-asset flows dominating the tape, my focus is now on the yen crosses as they react to shifting fundamental data. As Justin Low from our team recently analyzed, the BOJ is widely expected to deliver another 25-basis-point hike by year-end, meaning any reversion toward the weekly VWAP will create fresh volatility for traders defending the USD/JPY 160 handle.

What Alphabet’s earnings mean for the Nasdaq outlook

Alphabet delivered a powerful operating quarter, but the market reaction shows that strong growth is no longer the only standard investors are applying to major AI companies.

The company reported second-quarter revenue of $119.8 billion, up 24% from a year earlier. Google Cloud revenue accelerated 82% to $24.8 billion, while operating income rose 30%. These figures confirm that enterprise demand for AI infrastructure and cloud capacity remains extremely strong. Alphabet’s official earnings release

However, Alphabet also recorded approximately $44.9 billion in quarterly capital expenditure, contributing to negative free cash flow of roughly $5.9 billion. Management raised its 2026 capital expenditure forecast to $195 billion-$205 billion, above its previous $180 billion-$190 billion range. Alphabet shares consequently traded roughly 2%-3% lower after hours.

The reported $112.1 billion of net income also requires context. Approximately $98 billion of other income came mainly from unrealized gains on equity investments. That means the headline profit figure significantly overstates the underlying quarterly earnings power of Alphabet’s operating businesses.

For Nasdaq traders, the report carries two competing messages.

The constructive interpretation is that AI demand remains exceptionally strong. Rapid cloud growth and continued infrastructure investment may support semiconductor companies, data-center suppliers and other businesses connected to the AI capital-spending cycle.

The more cautious interpretation is that the cost of competing in AI is rising rapidly. Investors now have to ask not only whether AI demand is growing, but how much cash must be reinvested to capture that demand and when those investments will produce acceptable returns.

Alphabet’s earnings are therefore bullish for the AI demand story but mixed for mega-cap technology valuations. That distinction matters for the Nasdaq, where expectations are already high and companies can report excellent revenue growth without producing a positive stock reaction.

Nasdaq futures prediction score: -3 out of 10

The current Nasdaq futures prediction score is -3, representing a modest bearish advantage rather than a high-confidence breakdown call.

The score reflects four main factors:

  • Accepted value has migrated lower over several sessions.
  • Two rallies failed in the 29,295-29,365 resistance region.
  • Nasdaq futures remain below important short-term and 4-hour resistance.
  • Buyers have responded near 29,030, reducing the risk of an immediate uncontrolled decline.

The score is a snapshot of the current market structure. It is not the same as tradeability and it does not mean that every trader should be short. Entry location, confirmation, timeframe and risk tolerance remain important.

Why has the Nasdaq futures outlook weakened?

Nasdaq futures previously rallied from below 28,800 to approximately 29,365. The important development was not simply that the rally stopped, but how the market behaved near the high.

The first test of approximately 29,365 attracted unusually heavy trading activity, yet buyers could not establish sustained acceptance above the area. A later recovery reached approximately 29,340 and failed again.

That created a two-stage rejection zone between 29,295 and 29,365.

After the second failure, the market’s main areas of accepted trading moved progressively lower:

  • An earlier session developed value around 29,160-29,360.
  • The next session shifted value down toward 29,125-29,295.
  • The latest developing value area moved lower again, toward approximately 29,030-29,190.

The main high-volume reference also migrated from approximately 29,310 and 29,270 to around 29,075-29,100.

What this means: Price did not merely produce a brief downward wick. Traders began conducting more business and spending more time at lower prices. That is evidence of lower acceptance and gives sellers the short-term structural advantage.

Is the rebound from 29,030 a bullish reversal?

Not yet, although it is a credible recovery attempt.

Buyers responded near 29,030, pushed price back above 29,100, and produced a more efficient rebound than the preceding decline. That response matters because it shows that sellers have not achieved uncontested control below the lower edge of the current value area.

However, the rebound remains below several layers of resistance:

  • 29,125-29,130: First recovery checkpoint
  • 29,157-29,195: Breakdown origin and upper edge of current value
  • 29,220: Important prior high-volume reference
  • 29,255-29,295: Stronger recovery and rejection zone
  • 29,310-29,365: Major distribution area

This is why the evidence should be adjudicated as bearish structure with an active recovery attempt, rather than either a confirmed breakdown or a bullish takeover.

The newest intraday evidence is also provisional because the latest recovery bar was still developing at the analysis cutoff.

Nasdaq bullish above 29,195

The bullish tradeCompass scenario activates above 29,195.

This threshold is placed just beyond the upper edge of the current accepted-value area. A sustained move above it would indicate that buyers are beginning to recover territory lost during the latest decline.

Bullish areas to watch are:

  1. 29,215 - The first reaction area near the previous session’s main high-volume price.
  2. 29,250 - Initial resistance ahead of the 4-hour resistance ribbon.
  3. 29,290 - The lower edge of the latest major rejection zone.
  4. 29,330 - A high-volume resistance shelf beneath the recent peak.
  5. 29,365 - The major 4-hour breakout and invalidation level for the lower-high pattern.

There is an important distinction between activation and confirmation.

A move above 29,195 activates the early bullish recovery scenario. The evidence becomes more convincing only if Nasdaq futures also reclaim and defend 29,220-29,260. A stronger bullish takeover would require acceptance above 29,295-29,310, followed eventually by a 4-hour close above 29,365.

If price briefly crosses 29,195 but quickly falls back below approximately 29,175, the breakout should be treated cautiously. That would suggest buyers touched the threshold without securing acceptance above it.

What this means: Acceptance requires more than a momentary price spike. Traders should look for price to remain above the level, defend a pullback or close above it on their chosen confirmation timeframe.

Nasdaq bearish below 29,020

The bearish tradeCompass scenario activates below 29,020.

This threshold sits beneath the present defense area around 29,030-29,035. A sustained break below it would show that sellers have pushed Nasdaq futures out of the current value area and invalidated the latest recovery attempt.

Bearish areas to watch are:

  1. 28,960 - The first target and an area where traders should anticipate a possible reaction.
  2. 28,950 - A major structural level from the previous bullish map.
  3. 28,860 - Secondary support from the prior auction.
  4. 28,775 - A deeper reaction area near earlier support.
  5. 28,700 - Major 4-hour range support.

A brief move below 29,020 is not enough by itself. The market may sweep through the visible low, trigger stops and then recover.

A cleaner bearish confirmation would include one of the following:

  • A 30-minute close below 29,020
  • Sustained trading below the level
  • A breakdown followed by a failed retest from underneath
  • A move below 28,950 that cannot recover promptly

If 28,700 eventually fails, the broader rebound from 28,408 would suffer more serious technical damage and the probability of revisiting that low would increase.

Where is the cleaner Nasdaq short scenario?

The cleaner short location may not be at the current price.

Nasdaq futures are already close to support around 29,020-29,030, which makes selling directly into the lower boundary less attractive before it breaks. Responsive buyers have already demonstrated an interest in defending this area.

A failed rebound into 29,185-29,220 could provide a more informative bearish test. Traders would then watch whether price can hold above the resistance zone or immediately rotate back below approximately 29,157-29,175.

A higher rebound into 29,255-29,310 would test a more important supply area. Failure there would preserve the lower-high structure, while sustained acceptance would weaken the bearish thesis.

This does not mean every test of resistance is automatically a short. The reaction after the test matters. A resistance level becomes less useful to sellers when price begins holding above it and defending pullbacks.

What does the 4-hour Nasdaq chart show?

The 4-hour chart supports a neutral-bearish interpretation.

The rebound from 28,408 remains technically intact, but it stalled at 29,365 and is now at risk of forming a lower high. Nasdaq futures are also trading below a declining resistance ribbon around 29,210-29,260.

The immediate 4-hour battle is therefore:

  • Support:29,025-29,050
  • Resistance:29,210-29,260

Below support, the next major areas are 28,900, 28,800 and 28,700.

Above resistance, Nasdaq futures would still have to clear 29,295-29,365 before the broader recovery could be considered fully restored.

Because the latest 4-hour candle was incomplete at the analysis cutoff, its closing location carries more weight than an intrabar move through either boundary.

Nasdaq futures support and resistance levels to watch

What many Nasdaq traders may get wrong

The first mistake would be assuming that Alphabet’s strong revenue and cloud growth must automatically lift the Nasdaq. The after-hours reaction demonstrates that the market is also evaluating free cash flow, capital intensity, expectations and valuation.

The second mistake would be chasing a short directly into 29,020-29,030 before sellers establish acceptance below support.

The third would be treating a rebound above 29,100 as proof that buyers have regained control. That level is close to current fair value. The more meaningful tests are 29,195, 29,220-29,260 and ultimately 29,295-29,365.

Finally, traders should avoid switching direction on every small move inside the decision zone. The area between 29,020 and 29,195 can produce rotations, false breaks and repeated tests before the market chooses a clearer direction.

How traders can use the Nasdaq tradeCompass

The investingLive tradeCompass defines one bullish threshold, one bearish threshold and the decision zone between them. It is intended to help traders respond to confirmation instead of predicting every candle.

For this map:

  • Above 29,195: The early bullish recovery scenario activates.
  • Above 29,220-29,260: The recovery gains stronger confirmation.
  • Above 29,295-29,365: The bearish lower-high thesis is progressively invalidated.
  • Below 29,020: The latest buyer response begins to fail.
  • Below 28,950: The bearish structure becomes more convincing.
  • Below 28,700: The broader rebound from 28,408 is materially damaged.

After the first target is reached, traders can consider taking partial profits or reducing risk. After the second target, protecting the remaining position becomes increasingly important. A profitable setup should not be allowed to turn into a full loss simply because the trader hoped for the most distant target.

One trade per direction is another useful discipline. Once the best part of a planned move has already occurred, repeatedly entering the same direction can turn a good market read into overtrading.

How to know if this Nasdaq analysis is still valid

This analysis remains relevant while Nasdaq futures continue reacting around 29,020-29,195 and the broader 28,950-29,365 structure.

If price has already moved well beyond a threshold and reached several targets, the map should not be treated as a fresh entry signal. Instead, traders can use it to judge whether the move is holding, becoming overextended or failing back through the breakout level.

Alphabet’s earnings are an important catalyst, but price remains the final adjudicator. A sustained recovery above 29,195 would reduce the present bearish tone. Acceptance above 29,220-29,260 would improve it further. Conversely, a failure below 29,020, particularly if followed by acceptance below 28,950, would confirm that sellers remain in control.

Trade at your own risk. This Nasdaq futures analysis is an educational decision map, not financial advice or a guarantee of future results.

This article was written by Itai Levitan at investinglive.com.

item.title: BOJ expected to raise interest rates again by end of the year - poll
item.description:
The survey was conducted on 13-21 July, so it will have accounted for the latest US-Iran developments for the most part. These are some of the key findings:

  • 83 of 87 economists expect BOJ to leave interest rates unchanged this quarter
  • 75 of 87 economists expect BOJ to deliver another 25 bps rate hike to 1.25% by end-December
  • 27 of 51 economists expect that rate hike to be in December, while 18 of 51 economists expect a move in October
  • 23 of 32 economists said BOJ was not moving too slowly on rate hikes
  • 23 of 29 economists believe that USD/JPY around 160 is "too weak" relative to Japan's economic fundamentals

I think the expectation of the next move by the BOJ is a fair one, largely keeping with market pricing as well. As things stand, traders are pricing in ~25 bps of rate hikes by the BOJ by year-end.

At this stage, I would argue that a move in either October or December is very much a toss up. A lot will also depend on how things play out with regards to the Middle East situation.

Adding to potential inflation complications now is the weak Japanese yen currency. The BOJ might feel more compelled to take action with the currency being down in the doldrums as that could acceleration price pressures in the Japanese economy. As such, an earlier move could be an option in order to curb such inflationary pressures - should the opportunity present itself that is.

As for the ~80% of respondents believing that USD/JPY at 160 being "too weak", that is quite an interesting one. While the path of least resistance remains for a move higher in the currency pair, how much exactly is too much given the market moves since October? It definitely does warrant some consideration.

But then again, there is nothing in terms of fundamental developments to really suggest a turnaround in sentiment for the yen currency.

And when you take that into consideration, it's tough to really say that even at fresh 40-year lows that the yen is "too weak" i.e. USD/JPY is "too high".

This article was written by Justin Low at investinglive.com.

Middle East tensions dominated markets again, with Brent crude holding near a six week high as the US and Iran traded strikes for a 12th straight night. CENTCOM confirmed the latest round of attacks on Iranian military targets was ordered directly by President Trump, aimed at further degrading Iran's ability to threaten commercial shipping, following Tuesday's use of a B-1 long-range bomber, the first such mission since this phase of the conflict began 12 days ago. Reports from Axios and the Wall Street Journal added that Washington is surging special forces, jets and medics into the region alongside an extra $73bln in war funding, underscoring how quickly the conflict is escalating on the ground even as diplomatic channels through Qatar remain open.

The other major thread overnight was the widening threat to shipping. Iran's Revolutionary Guards declared the Strait of Hormuz fully closed, warning no tanker will transit without their coordination and threatening to halt oil flows entirely if Iranian infrastructure comes under attack, a claim that followed reports of one tanker catching fire and two others turning back near the strait's mined southern route. Simultaneously, the Houthis extended their own campaign into the Red Sea, claiming strikes on the Saudi tankers Layla and Encelia, though UKMTO said only one vessel had actually been hit. Around 9 to 10 ships have now abandoned plans to transit Bab el-Mandeb, and Kuwait reported intercepting drones over its own airspace, a sign the conflict's shipping and airspace risks are spreading beyond the two original chokepoints. Gold's pullback on the news marked a reversion to a more conventional risk reaction, even as the US dollar softened modestly against most peers.

That said, not every part of the market was in risk-off mode. Asian equities extended a sharp rally, with the Kospi up more than 3% and the Nikkei around 1% higher, as Google's raised full year capex guidance of $195bln to $205bln, alongside strong Tesla earnings, reinforced the view that AI infrastructure spending remains firmly intact, a boon for chipmakers including SK Hynix and Samsung. Australia added its own data point to the mix, with June employment surging 76.3k against a 15k forecast. item.title: US deploys B-1 bomber against Iran in biggest strike escalation yet
item.description:
The use of a B-1 bomber, the first since fighting with Iran resumed, marks a clear step up in the scale of US strikes and signals Washington may be preparing for a broader campaign rather than the more limited strikes seen in recent days. That escalation risk, layered on top of an unresolved standoff over the Strait of Hormuz and a fresh Houthi attack on Saudi shipping, keeps a substantial geopolitical premium embedded in oil prices and raises the risk of a sharper supply disruption across two major chokepoints at once. Ongoing Qatari mediated talks aimed at reopening the strait offer a potential de-escalation path, but reports that Iran has not accepted the latest proposal suggest markets should not expect a near term resolution. With Trump still weighing a return to major combat operations that officials say could come within days, volatility in oil and regional risk assets is likely to stay elevated.

--- A first B-1 bomber strike on Iran signals the war could be entering a far more intense phase, even as mediators scramble to reopen Hormuz.

Summary:

  • US military used a B-1 long-range bomber Tuesday to strike IRGC targets in Iran, the first B-1 mission since fighting resumed 12 days ago
  • The B-1 can carry two dozen 2,000lb bombs or dozens of cruise missiles and flies faster than sound at low altitude
  • CENTCOM's public statement on Tuesday's strikes did not mention the B-1 mission specifically
  • Trump is still weighing a return to major combat operations against Iran, which US and Israeli officials say could happen within days
  • Houthi rebels attacked Saudi ships for the first time since declaring a blockade, which a US official said may be Iran directed to open a new front in the Red Sea
  • Qatari mediators continue talks with US, Iranian and Omani officials on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, though Iran has reportedly not accepted the latest proposal

The US military used a B-1 long-range bomber on Tuesday to strike Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targets inside Iran, the first time a B-1 has flown a mission since fighting between the two countries resumed 12 days ago, according to Axios, which cited US officials. The bomber, capable of carrying roughly two dozen 2,000 pound bombs or dozens of cruise missiles and flying faster than sound at low altitude, represents the largest bomb load of any bomber in the US arsenal, and its deployment signals a notable expansion of the campaign against Iran.

The mission launched from an airbase in the UK and was tracked by online plane spotting sites. Notably, US Central Command's public statement on Tuesday's strikes did not mention the B-1 mission, instead describing attacks on Iranian military operations centers, maritime capabilities, aircraft hangars, drone storage facilities and logistics infrastructure aimed at degrading Iran's ability to threaten shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. It remains unclear what specific targets the B-1 hit or whether the mission proved more effective than other recent strikes. The US flew similar B-1 missions during the earlier phase of the conflict known as Operation Epic Fury, hitting missile bases, command centers, weapons storage sites and air defense systems.

Despite the expanded strikes, Iran has shown no sign of shifting its position on the Strait of Hormuz and continues to target US bases in the region, with officials divided over how much military capability Iran retains near the strait. President Trump has threatened to bomb bridges and power plants, including in Tehran, if Iran attacks further vessels there, prompting Iran to threaten infrastructure in Gulf countries allied with Washington. Separately, Houthi rebels struck Saudi ships for the first time since declaring their blockade, a move a US defense official suggested may be directed by Iran to open a second pressure point in the Red Sea alongside the Gulf, prompting several vessels to divert away from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

Qatari mediators are continuing talks with US, Iranian and Omani officials in an effort to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and halt the fighting, though a regional source said Iranian leadership has not accepted the latest proposal on the table. Trump, speaking in Georgia on Wednesday night, suggested Iran was under heavy pressure and might eventually seek a deal, but expressed skepticism about the durability of any near term agreement. With US forces continuing to build up in the region and Trump still weighing a full return to major combat operations, officials on both the US and Israeli sides say that scenario could unfold within days. 

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Kospi jumps 3%, Nikkei rises as Google's AI capex boost lifts chip stocks
item.description:
The rally in Korean and Japanese equities underscores how directly Asian chipmakers are now leveraged to the US hyperscaler capex cycle, with Google's raised full year spending guidance validating expectations that AI infrastructure demand still has further to run. SK Hynix and Samsung's outsized gains point to markets pricing sustained strength in memory and advanced chip demand tied to data centre build outs, a read-through likely to extend to other regional semiconductor suppliers in coming sessions. South Korea's GDP beat adds a domestic growth tailwind on top of the AI driven rally, though it also raises the odds of further Bank of Korea tightening, a dynamic that could complicate the equity story if higher rates start to weigh on valuations. As a broader risk sentiment gauge, the strength in Asian equities is a modestly supportive backdrop for risk sensitive currencies including the Australian dollar, though FX moves in the region look more idiosyncratic today and are worth covering separately.

--- Google's bigger AI spending bill is rippling through Asia, sending Korean and Japanese chip stocks sharply higher.

Summary:

  • Kospi rose more than 3%, its third straight advance, led by SK Hynix up 6.5% and Samsung Electronics up 4.8%
  • Nikkei rose around 1% as Asian markets tracked the AI capex rally
  • Google raised its full year capex guidance to between $195bln and $205bln, reinforcing expectations AI infrastructure spending remains robust
  • Alphabet and Tesla earnings both pointed to continued heavy AI infrastructure investment
  • South Korea's Q2 GDP grew 0.6% quarter on quarter, ahead of the 0.4% forecast, on strong chip exports
  • LG Energy Solution also rose almost 4% on the day

South Korean and Japanese shares rallied on Thursday, with the Kospi surging more than 3% and the Nikkei adding around 1%, as Google's decision to raise its full year capital expenditure guidance reinforced expectations that the AI infrastructure spending boom still has plenty of room to run. The Kospi's advance marked a third consecutive session of gains, taking the index up more than 7% over that stretch, though it remains sharply below its record close from late June.

Chipmakers led the charge in Seoul, with SK Hynix rising as much as 6.5% and Samsung Electronics gaining 4.8%, while battery maker LG Energy Solution climbed almost 4%. The moves came after Google lifted its full year capex forecast to a range of $195bln to $205bln, a figure that, alongside robust Tesla earnings, reassured markets that hyperscaler spending on AI infrastructure is not slowing. That spending flows directly into demand for the advanced logic and memory chips that Korean suppliers produce for data centres, making Kospi heavyweights among the most direct regional beneficiaries of the AI capex cycle.

South Korea's own economic data added further support, with Asia's fourth largest economy expanding 0.6% quarter on quarter in the April to June period, ahead of a median forecast of 0.4% and driven largely by strong chip exports. That represented a sharp slowdown from 1.8% growth in the first quarter, but was still enough to suggest chip led momentum can continue underpinning growth even as policymakers begin a tightening cycle.

In Japan, the Nikkei's more modest gain reflected similar AI driven optimism, with the broader rally in Asian equities extending to the MSCI Asia-Pacific index outside Japan, which was tracking toward a solid weekly advance after two consecutive weekly declines. Currency moves in both South Korea and Japan were also notable on the day, though those developments are better addressed in a separate wrap given the scale of today's equity story. For now, the read-through from Alphabet's spending plans looks like the dominant driver across Asian markets, with chipmakers set to remain in focus as more hyperscaler earnings land in the weeks ahead. 

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Australia jobs smash forecasts, keeping RBA's August hike door (very slightly) open
item.description:
The blowout employment number and jump in participation gives the RBA scope to keep its hawkish bias alive without committing to actual policy tightening, and markets reacted accordingly, with the Australian dollar jumping and short term yields rising around 5bp on the data. The move in the yield reflects a modest repricing of hike risk into the August 11-12 meeting, though the quarterly average unemployment rate of 4.4%, still above the RBA's own 4.2% forecast, alongside underemployment and underutilisation both sitting at multi-month highs, complicates a clean hawkish read. On balance, another 25bp hike in August looks a lower probability outcome than the report's headline strength might suggest, given the RBA has already held steady in June after three consecutive hikes earlier in the year. Still, the scale of the beat is likely to keep a hike priced as a live possibility until closer to the meeting.

--- A blowout June jobs report has AUD and yields jumping, keeping an August RBA hike alive even if it's not the most likely outcome.

Summary:

  • Employment rose 76.3k in June, the strongest gain in over 12 months and far above the 15k expected
  • Unemployment rate held steady at 4.4%, matching expectations
  • Full time employment rose 29.3k and part time employment rose 47.0k
  • Participation rate rose to 67.0% from 66.7%, aided by a jump in 55 to 64 year old participation
  • Quarterly average unemployment of 4.4% sits above the RBA's 4.2% forecast, while underemployment at 6.5% and underutilisation at 10.9% hit 22-month and 54-month highs respectively
  • AUD jumped and the three year yield rose around 5bp on the data, with the next RBA meeting on August 11 and 12

Australia's labour market delivered its strongest employment gain in more than a year in June, smashing expectations and keeping the door open to a further Reserve Bank rate hike even as several details in the report complicate that picture. Employment rose 76.3k, far exceeding forecasts of 15k and building on an upwardly revised May gain, while the unemployment rate held steady at 4.4%, in line with expectations.

Full time employment rose 29.3k and part time employment increased 47.0k, while the participation rate jumped to 67.0% from 66.7%, a move driven largely by a surge in participation among 55 to 64 year olds. Hours worked rose 0.2% on the month and 0.5% over the quarter. On the surface, the report looks like a solidly strong outcome that reinforces the RBA's hawkish bias without forcing its hand. Some of the strength reflects a larger than usual number of people who were waiting to start a new job in May, a factor that flattered the headline number, while the jump in participation similarly reflects a specific cohort effect rather than a broad based shift.

Even so, the quarterly average unemployment rate of 4.4% remains above the RBA's own forecast of 4.2%, and following data revisions, both the underemployment rate at 6.5% and the underutilisation rate at 10.9% now sit at 22-month and 54-month highs respectively, pointing to more slack beneath the surface than the headline strength suggests. Taken together with the stronger employment print, however, the RBA could still conclude the labour market retains some underlying momentum.

The Australian dollar jumped on the release and short term yields moved higher, as markets adjusted to the prospect of continued RBA hawkishness. The central bank raised rates by 25bp at each of its first three meetings this year before holding steady at its June meeting, and the next decision falls on August 11 and 12. While this report keeps a further hike in play, the combination of a June pause, elevated underemployment and a quarterly unemployment rate still running above the RBA's forecast makes another move at the August meeting look a less likely outcome than the headline number alone might imply. 

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Oil hits six-week high as US strikes Iran, Houthis blockade Saudi ports
item.description:
Oil's push to a fresh six week high reflects a rapidly escalating risk premium as two of the world's most important chokepoints, the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb, both face active threats to shipping in the same session. Iran's claim of control over the Hormuz route, and its warning that tankers cannot pass without coordination, raises the prospect of a de facto disruption to a corridor carrying a substantial share of global crude and LNG flows, even before any confirmed stoppage in actual throughput. The Houthi blockade declaration against Saudi Arabia adds a second, largely independent threat vector in the Red Sea, compounding insurance and freight costs for tankers regardless of which route they attempt. The build in US crude stocks, against expectations for a draw, is likely to be overshadowed entirely by the geopolitical headlines, and risk sensitive currencies including the Australian dollar are likely to stay on the back foot while the conflict shows signs of widening rather than de-escalating.

--- Oil is surging on twin flashpoints, a claimed Iranian lockdown of Hormuz and a Houthi blockade of Saudi Arabia, as the risk premium builds fast.

Summary:

  • Brent crude rose to around $96 a barrel, a six week high, while WTI rose to around $88, both up roughly 2%
  • US carried out a 12th consecutive night of strikes on Iran
  • Trump has vowed to destroy an Iranian bridge or power plant for every attack on a ship in the Strait of Hormuz
  • Iran's Revolutionary Guards say the Strait of Hormuz is under their control and completely closed, warning tankers need Iranian coordination to transit
  • Houthis claim to have struck Saudi tankers including the Encelia and forced around 10 vessels to retreat, declaring a naval blockade of Saudi Arabia
  • US crude stocks rose by around 2 million barrels last week versus an expected draw, according to EIA data

Oil prices jumped to their highest level in more than six weeks on Thursday, as a fresh round of US strikes on Iran and an escalating Houthi campaign against Saudi shipping combined to push a heavy risk premium back into crude markets. Brent crude climbed to around $96 a barrel, up roughly 2% and its strongest level since early June, building on a similarly sharp gain in the prior session. US West Texas Intermediate rose to around $88, also up close to 2%, extending Wednesday's near 3% advance.

The US military confirmed a 12th consecutive night of strikes on Iran, coming hours after President Trump reiterated his warning that Washington would destroy an Iranian bridge or power plant for every attack Iran carries out on a vessel transiting the Strait of Hormuz. That threat marks a further escalation in a conflict that, as previously reported, has already surpassed $37bln in cost and drawn a growing US military buildup across the region.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said an oil tanker had caught fire after an explosion while attempting to cross what they described as a mined route south of the strait, and that two further tankers had turned back. The Guards said the waterway was now under their control and effectively closed, warning that no vessel would be permitted to enter or exit without coordinating with Iran, a claim that, if sustained, would represent a major escalation given the strait's role as a corridor for roughly a fifth of global oil shipments in normal conditions.

Adding to the pressure, the Iran aligned Houthis have opened a second front by threatening vessels carrying Saudi oil through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and declaring a naval blockade of Saudi Arabia, consistent with the group's own recent statements claiming strikes on the Saudi flagged tankers Encelia and Layla. Maritime security reports indicated the Encelia had indeed been hit in the Red Sea, and the Houthis said they had forced around 10 vessels to abandon plans to sail to Saudi ports, an account Reuters said it could not independently verify. Iran's Revolutionary Guards separately warned shipping companies via social media that the southern Hormuz route is mined.

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7712 – Reuters estimate
item.description:
The People’s Bank of China is due to set the daily USD/CNY reference rate at around 0115 GMT (2115 US Eastern time), a fixing that remains one of the most closely watched signals in Asian foreign exchange markets. China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, under which the renminbi (yuan) is allowed to trade within a prescribed band around a central reference rate, or midpoint, set each trading day by the PBOC. The current trading band permits the currency to move plus or minus 2% from the official midpoint during onshore trading hours. Each morning, the PBOC determines the midpoint based on a range of inputs. These include the previous day’s closing price, movements in major currencies, particularly the US dollar, broader international FX conditions, and domestic economic considerations such as capital flows, growth momentum and financial stability objectives. The midpoint is not a purely mechanical calculation, allowing policymakers discretion to guide market expectations. Once the midpoint is announced, onshore USD/CNY is free to trade within the allowable band. If market pressures push the yuan toward either edge of that range, the central bank may step in to smooth volatility. Intervention can take the form of direct buying or selling of yuan, adjustments to liquidity conditions, or guidance through state-owned banks. As a result, the daily fixing is often interpreted as a policy signal rather than just a technical reference point. A stronger-than-expected CNY midpoint is typically read as a sign the PBOC is leaning against depreciation pressure, while a weaker fixing for the CNY can indicate tolerance for a softer currency, often in response to dollar strength or domestic economic headwinds.In periods of heightened global volatility, such as shifts in US rate expectations, trade tensions or capital flow pressures, the fixing takes on added significance. For investors, it provides insight into Beijing’s currency priorities, balancing competitiveness, capital stability and financial market confidence.

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: US Trade Rep. Greer eyes interim US deals with Canada, Mexico by year end
item.description:
Signs of a delayed, piecemeal approach to USMCA renegotiation add to the uncertainty already weighing on North American trade flows, particularly for autos, steel and aluminum exporters awaiting relief from Section 232 tariffs. Markets are likely to view an interim deal with Mexico as more achievable near term, given Mexico's direct engagement in bilateral talks, while a genuine breakthrough with Canada looks harder to square with Trump's freshly imposed 50% tariff on a swathe of Canadian goods this same week. That escalation raises real questions over how credible Greer's timeline for a Canada arrangement by year end actually is, and whether Ottawa's exclusion from the Mexico talks leaves it with little leverage to negotiate better terms. The prospect of tougher rules of origin and labor standards slipping into 2027 also prolongs the investment uncertainty already weighing on regional manufacturing decisions.

--- Washington is angling for quick interim trade patches with Mexico and Canada, even as a fresh 50% tariff on Canadian goods clouds the path to any deal with Ottawa.

Summary:

  • US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer says he hopes for interim deals with Canada and Mexico by year end
  • Harder USMCA issues, including autos rules of origin and labor and environmental standards, pushed into 2027 talks with Congress
  • Mexico and Canada are seeking relief from Trump's Section 232 tariffs of 25% on autos and 50% on steel and aluminum
  • Canada excluded from bilateral USMCA talks in Mexico City, raising the risk it must accept terms set by Mexico
  • Trump this week imposed a 50% tariff on about $20bln of Canadian goods, including beer, dairy and hockey sticks
  • Trump declined to renew USMCA on 1 July, triggering a 10 year countdown to its expiration absent a renewal agreement

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said on Wednesday he hopes to secure interim trade arrangements with Mexico and Canada before the end of the year, while pushing thornier changes to the US Mexico Canada Agreement into 2027, according to Reuters. Testifying before the Senate Finance Committee, Greer said he would like to have some arrangement in place with each country, though he offered no specifics on what such deals might look like.

Greer said tougher issues, including tighter rules of origin for autos and labor and environmental standards, would likely require further discussion with Congress next year, effectively confirming that a full USMCA renewal will not happen in 2026. Mexico's Economy Ministry declined to comment on his remarks, and Canada's trade ministry did not immediately respond. One trade adviser said Greer's testimony confirms Washington is no longer pursuing a clean renewal this year, and predicted the likely outcome is an interim political arrangement that leaves the hardest issues, and much of the investment uncertainty, unresolved.

Both Mexico and Canada are seeking relief from the Section 232 national security tariffs Trump imposed last year, 25% on autos and 50% on steel and aluminum. Greer was due in Mexico City for bilateral talks with Mexican officials, while Canada has been excluded from those negotiations, raising the risk Ottawa is left to accept whatever terms Mexico agrees to. Washington is also pressing Mexico to raise North American content requirements for vehicles to qualify for preferential access, and has tied progress on a Mexico deal to non-trade issues including border security and compliance with a decades old water sharing treaty.

Whether a Canada arrangement materialises on anything like Greer's timeline looks considerably less certain, however. His testimony came in the same week Trump slapped a 50% tariff on roughly $20bln of Canadian goods, including beer, dairy and hockey sticks, in retaliation for Ottawa's own countermeasures, a move that sits awkwardly alongside talk of an imminent interim deal and underscores how strained the US Canada trade relationship has become just as Trump's decision not to renew USMCA starts a 10 year countdown to its expiration.

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Preview: Westpac, CBA see steady June jobs data but flag rising labour market slack
item.description:
A steady headline unemployment rate would offer only limited reassurance to the RBA given both banks' emphasis on broader signs of labour market slack building beneath the surface. Westpac's focus on a corrected underemployment series showing a material rise, rather than the previously reported sideways trend, points to a softer underlying jobs picture than earlier data suggested. CBA's flagged risk of a downside surprise to 4.3% could briefly support the case for a more dovish RBA reading, though both banks agree the medium term trend is toward gradually higher unemployment.

For the Australian dollar, a steady headline print is likely to be a non-event, but any softer than expected outcome, particularly a dip toward 4.3% or weaker underemployment detail, would likely weigh on the currency by reinforcing bets on a more dovish (or at least less hawkish) RBA path. With CBA noting unemployment would still sit above the RBA's own 4.2% forecast for the June quarter, the data keeps pressure on the central bank to reconcile its outlook with incoming figures, a dynamic AUD traders are likely to stay sensitive to into the next RBA meeting.

Earlier:

  • Economic and event calendar in Asia - Australian jobs report

Westpac and CBA both see steady June jobs numbers on the surface, but warn of building slack beneath, led by rising underemployment.

Summary:

  • Westpac and CBA both forecast June employment to rise 15k with unemployment steady at 4.4%
  • Both expect the participation rate to hold at 66.7%
  • Westpac says a corrected ABS underemployment series, following a reported systems error, shows underemployment rising materially rather than moving sideways
  • Westpac points to new unofficial underemployment measures also lifting well above the official rate
  • CBA flags a risk unemployment could round down to 4.3%, but says leading indicators point to a gradual rise in unemployment over the rest of 2026
  • CBA notes its 4.4% forecast would still sit above the RBA's own 4.2% estimate for the June quarter, though this is not yet a major concern for the central bank

Economists at Westpac and Commonwealth Bank of Australia both expect Australia's June labour force data to show employment rising by 15,000 and the unemployment rate holding at 4.4%, but each is warning that softer signals beneath the headline numbers point to a labour market losing momentum.

Westpac said the May labour force survey had given a clearer read on the underlying trend now that recent sources of noise had faded, and argued genuine weakness is starting to form after employment growth effectively stalled over April and May. The bank noted employment had expanded around 26,000 a month in the first quarter before that stalling took hold, leaving the employment to population ratio 0.7 percentage points below its recent high. Westpac also flagged that the Bureau of Statistics had disclosed a systems error in its initial May release that had produced incorrect underemployment figures. Once corrected, Westpac said, those figures materially change the picture, showing underemployment rising rather than moving broadly sideways as first thought, a shift reinforced by newer unofficial underemployment measures that have climbed well ahead of the official rate. Westpac argued that both weaker demand for labour and cost of living pressures affecting supply are likely contributing, and that persistence in these trends would build the case for broader slack across the labour market.

CBA struck a similar tone on the headline numbers, forecasting unemployment to hold at 4.4% and the participation rate to stay unchanged, while acknowledging a risk that unemployment could round down to 4.3% given how close the current rate sits to that threshold. The bank pointed to leading indicators including capacity utilisation and job advertisements as evidence of a gradual upward trend in unemployment through the rest of the year. CBA noted its 4.4% projection would remain below its own and the RBA's estimate of the non-accelerating inflation rate of unemployment, but still well above the central bank's most recent forecast of a 4.2% average for the June quarter. The bank said this gradual drift higher is unlikely to unsettle the RBA in the near term, given unemployment remains low by historical standards and sits below estimates of full employment.

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.
